## 4 December 2020

## Circular to management companies of SFC-authorised real estate investment trusts

## Streamlined approach for vetting and approval of announcements and circulars

1. The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) informs management companies of SFC-authorised real estate investment trusts (REITs) of the streamlined approach for vetting and approval of announcements and circulars under 10.2 of the Code on Real Estate Investment Trusts (REIT Code) with effect from 4 December 2020.

## Background

2. Under 10.2 of the REIT Code, all announcements, circulars and notices of an SFCauthorised REIT shall be submitted to the SFC for prior approval before they are issued.
3. It has been our long-established policy to regulate REITs in the same manner as listed companies.  With broad support received in the recent public consultation, the REIT Code has been revised to broadly align the requirements for REITs' connected party transactions and notifiable transactions with the requirements for listed companies. The amendments took effect today.
4. In view of these amendments, the SFC will align its practices for review of documents with those under the Listing Rules and adopt a streamlined approach to vetting and approving certain announcements and circulars under 10.2 of the REIT Code. This should facilitate more efficient management of SFC-authorised REITs and the timely dissemination of information on REITs. It also aims to promote REIT managers' selfcompliance without compromising investor protection.

## Streamlined approach

## Announcements and circulars

5. Subject to the paragraphs below, with effect from 4 December 2020, announcements and circulars to be issued by a REIT under the REIT Code need not be submitted to the SFC for pre-vetting before publication except where:
2. (a) such announcements or circulars, if issued by a listed company, are required to be submitted to The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (SEHK) for review before they are issued under the Listing Rules; or
3. (b) pre-vetting is specifically required under the REIT Code or other guidance published by the SFC from time to time, for example in the case of issue and redemption of perpetual bonds referred in Question 34 of Frequently Asked Questions relating to REITs.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

6. Notwithstanding the post-vetting approach adopted for certain announcements or circulars, REIT managers are reminded that where any matter covered by an announcement or a circular (such as proposed change in the management company or trustee of a REIT and classification of certain properties as Qualified Minority-owned Properties) is subject to the SFC's prior approval under the REIT Code, such approval must be obtained before the publication of the relevant announcement or circular.

## Filing and post-vetting

7. In respect of announcements or circulars which are not subject to pre-vetting by the SFC, REIT managers are required to file such announcements or circulars with the SFC immediately following their submission to SEHK for publication.
8. The SFC will conduct post-vetting of these announcements and circulars to monitor compliance. REIT managers should ensure that the SFC-authorised REITs under their management, and all disclosures made, are compliant with all relevant requirements set out in the REIT Code and the trust deeds constituting the REITs.
9. Notwithstanding the above, the SFC retains its power to require REIT managers to submit any announcement or circular for pre-vetting where the SFC considers it appropriate in individual cases.
10.  The SFC may make follow-up enquiries or take other regulatory action (including requiring a REIT manager to issue a clarification announcement or take other remedial action) as appropriate. REIT managers are expected to respond to any enquiries made by the SFC promptly and in an open and cooperative manner.

## Other

11.  We will review the operation and effectiveness of the streamlined approach and further changes may be considered where appropriate.
12.  Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.
